domain_label: Reasoning Enhancement & Test-Time Compute — Verification, Self-Correction & Anti-Hallucination
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope covers verifier/critic models, self-refine loops, process vs outcome reward models, tool-grounded checking, calibrated abstention, grounding checks
evaluation is accuracy and calibration centric unless project overrides
generator LLM is treated as a black box; only its outputs are verified
exclusions: adversarial robustness and jailbreaking beyond verification scope
general RLHF policy training beyond reward modeling

competency_questions.question: What verifier architecture separates generator from quality judge and how is the interface defined?
When should a fine-tuned critic model replace a zero-shot GPT-4 critic?
How does self-refine differ from self-consistency and when should each be used?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELF_REFINE vs SELFCONSIST covered with conflict axis CA_10

competency_questions.question: What are the stopping conditions for a self-refine loop to prevent error amplification?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELF_REFINE acceptance tests and EC_02 cover this

competency_questions.question: What is the difference between a Process Reward Model and an Outcome Reward Model and when should each be trained?
How is chain-of-thought verified step by step and what tools are used?
How does best-of-N selection work and what determines the optimal N?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BEST_OF_N defines selection and cost-quality tradeoff

competency_questions.question: What conditions cause self-consistency majority vote to fail?
How are factual hallucinations detected and attributed to specific claims?
How is RAG-generated output verified for faithfulness to retrieved passages?
How is model calibration measured and when should abstention be triggered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CALIB_ABSTAIN + CALIBR_EVAL define ECE and threshold

competency_questions.question: How is reward hacking detected and what triggers a human audit?
How are probability outputs verified for coherence and numeric correctness?
How are structural output requirements enforced without semantic content checking?

glossary.definition: reward model assigning scores to intermediate reasoning steps rather than final outputs
reward model scoring only the final answer or output quality
iterative generator-critique-regenerate loop where the same model critiques and improves its own output
sampling multiple independent reasoning chains and aggregating via majority vote
alignment between model confidence scores and empirical accuracy frequencies
model output containing factual claims not supported by training data or provided context
degree to which RAG-generated output is entailed by retrieved source passages
optimization process exploiting weaknesses in reward model to achieve high scores without genuine quality improvement
sampling N outputs and selecting the highest-scoring one according to a verifier or reward model
decoding algorithm that enforces output adheres to a grammar, schema, or regex at token generation time

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for verification and self-correction work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by Madaan et al. 2023 (Self-Refine) and Lightman et al. 2023 (Let's Verify Step by Step) as key reference works
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Madaan et al. 2023 arXiv:2303.17651; Lightman et al. 2023 arXiv:2305.20050

test_cases.input_summary: LLM output with injected factual error; verifier pipeline active
RM score high but human eval drops
self-refine loop iteration 3 worse than iteration 1

nodes.definition: Design and deploy a separate verifier or critic model that scores or critiques LLM outputs, distinct from the generator, to detect errors before surfacing to user.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new error taxonomy emerges or generator architecture changes

pros.claim: Separates generation from judgment, enabling independent quality control
pros.example: critic model rejects hallucinated citations before delivery

cons.claim: Doubles inference cost; verifier may share generator's blind spots
cons.example: shared pretraining data causes correlated errors

failure_modes: verifier collapses to always-accept
verifier-generator distribution mismatch
acceptance_tests: verifier catches >80% of injected factual errors on held-out set
false-positive rate <15% on known-correct outputs

nodes.definition: Implement iterative self-refine (Madaan et al. 2023): generator produces output, then self-critiques it, then regenerates improved output, cycling until acceptance criterion or budget exhausted.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: critique quality degrades or convergence rate drops

pros.claim: No external labels needed; leverage in-context feedback
pros.example: code refinement via self-critique improves pass@1 on HumanEval

cons.claim: Model may not catch its own systematic errors; latency multiplies with iterations
cons.example: GPT-4 self-critique misses subtle math reasoning flaws

failure_modes: infinite loop without termination guard
critique amplifies rather than corrects errors
acceptance_tests: refinement improves score on task metric vs single-pass baseline by >5%
loop terminates within budget on >95% of inputs

nodes.definition: Train a process reward model (Lightman et al. 2023 Let's Verify Step by Step) that assigns rewards to intermediate reasoning steps rather than final answer only, enabling fine-grained supervision of chain-of-thought.

included: reward assignment at each CoT step

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: step annotation taxonomy changes or math domain scope expands

pros.claim: Enables credit assignment to specific wrong steps; catches mid-chain errors
pros.example: PRM boosted MATH accuracy via best-of-N selection in Lightman 2023

cons.claim: Step annotation is expensive; annotation ambiguity at step boundaries
cons.example: annotators disagree on 'is this partial step correct?' 25% of the time

failure_modes: annotation inconsistency propagates to model
step segmentation ambiguity
acceptance_tests: PRM step-error detection F1 >0.70 on held-out math problems
PRM improves best-of-N selection accuracy vs ORM by >=3 pts

nodes.definition: Train an outcome reward model scoring only the final answer correctness, used for best-of-N selection and RLHF without step-level annotation cost.
inputs: ground truth or human preference labels

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: label distribution shifts or new answer type introduced

pros.claim: Lower annotation cost vs PRM; scales to diverse task types
pros.example: preference labels gathered from user ratings without step decomposition

cons.claim: No step-level signal; fails to localize errors within long chains
cons.example: ORM approves plausible-sounding but factually wrong medical advice

failure_modes: reward hacking: model produces superficially correct-looking wrong answers
ORM overfit to annotation artifacts
acceptance_tests: ORM best-of-N accuracy > single-sample baseline by >=2 pts
ORM rank correlation with human preference >0.70

nodes.definition: Generate N candidate outputs, score each with a verifier or reward model, select highest-scoring; trade compute for quality at inference time.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: verifier accuracy changes or compute budget revised

pros.claim: Orthogonal to training; leverages inference compute for quality uplift
pros.example: scaling N from 1 to 64 matches MATH accuracy of larger model in some regimes

cons.claim: N-fold inference cost; requires reliable verifier
cons.example: bad verifier picks N=1 worst instead of best

failure_modes: verifier scores poorly correlated with true quality; all N wrong
latency explosion when N not parallelized
acceptance_tests: best-of-N at N=16 outperforms N=1 by >=5% on target metric
selection latency meets SLA with N samples in parallel

nodes.definition: Ground factual claims in LLM outputs by executing external tool calls (calculator, code interpreter, search, database lookup) and comparing tool output to model assertions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tool suite changes or new claim types introduced

pros.claim: Deterministic external check anchors model in ground truth
pros.example: 2+2=5 claim rejected by calculator before user sees it

cons.claim: Only covers claims amenable to tool verification; latency and cost of tool calls
cons.example: open-ended historical claims cannot be calculator-verified

failure_modes: tool output itself erroneous
model ignores tool contradiction
tool unavailable at inference
acceptance_tests: tool contradiction detection recall >85% on injected numeric errors
pipeline halts on tool failure rather than silently passing

nodes.definition: Implement calibrated probability estimates on model outputs and define abstention policies: when model confidence is below threshold, decline to answer or escalate rather than hallucinate.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model updated or calibration distribution shifts

pros.claim: Prevents confident hallucinations; users prefer honest 'I don't know' over wrong answers
pros.example: medical QA: abstention on low-confidence diagnosis avoids patient harm

cons.claim: Calibration may not transfer across domains; abstention frustrates users on near-threshold cases
cons.example: calibrated model on MMLU uncalibrated on domain-specific legal corpus

failure_modes: overconfident model ignores calibration signal
abstention threshold too conservative, refusing valid queries
acceptance_tests: ECE <0.05 on held-out calibration set post temperature scaling
abstention rate matches expected uncertainty rate within 10% on eval set

nodes.definition: Elicit step-by-step reasoning traces from LLMs, then verify each reasoning step for logical consistency, factual correctness, and valid inference before accepting final answer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: CoT format changes or reasoning domain expands

pros.claim: Exposes intermediate work enabling targeted error detection
pros.example: step-by-step algebra verification catches sign errors before final answer

cons.claim: Long CoT chains multiply verification cost; hallucinated plausible steps hard to catch
cons.example: plausible-sounding wrong intermediate steps fool both model and verifier

failure_modes: correct steps leading to wrong conclusion
verifier misses subtle logical fallacies
acceptance_tests: step-verified answers show lower error rate than unverified on MATH and GSM8K benchmarks
step verification catches >=70% of known planted reasoning errors
revisit_triggers: verifier fails on new problem type

nodes.definition: Sample multiple independent reasoning chains for same query, aggregate answers via majority vote or weighted scoring; consistency across paths indicates reliability.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: sampling budget changes or task type shifts

pros.claim: No verifier training needed; purely inference-time quality boost
pros.example: Wang et al. 2023 self-consistency boosted GSM8K from 56% to 78% with greedy CoT base

cons.claim: K-fold inference cost; fails when all paths share the same systematic bias
cons.example: if model always makes the same algebraic mistake, majority vote returns wrong answer confidently

failure_modes: majority vote converges on same systematic error
diversity of chains collapses at low temperature
acceptance_tests: majority vote at K=20 outperforms greedy decode by >=3% on arithmetic benchmarks
low consistency score correlates with actual error rate (AUC>0.70)

nodes.definition: Build a hallucination detection pipeline: identify unsupported claims, entity errors, and fabricated references in LLM outputs using retrieval, NLI, or claim verification modules.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new hallucination taxonomy defined or knowledge base updated

pros.claim: Provides explainable attribution; surfacing specific unsupported claims builds user trust
pros.example: flagging 'paper X says Y' with no source stops fabricated citations

cons.claim: NLI errors propagate; open-domain claims lack reliable source coverage
cons.example: rare scientific facts lack retrievable sources even when correct

failure_modes: NLI model itself hallucinates entailment
unsupported claims labeled as supported due to superficial match
acceptance_tests: hallucination detection F1 >0.75 on FactScore-style benchmark
pipeline returns attribution for >90% of verifiable claims

nodes.definition: Verify that RAG-augmented outputs are grounded in retrieved context: check that claims in generated text are entailed by retrieved passages, flag extrapolations beyond context.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retrieval corpus changes or RAG prompt format revised

pros.claim: Closes the loop between retrieval and generation; prevents model adding unsourced facts
pros.example: medical RAG: every claim traced to specific guideline passage before presentation

cons.claim: Faithfulness scoring models imperfect; context may not cover all true facts
cons.example: faithful to wrong retrieved passage that itself contains error

failure_modes: model correct but context wrong; verifier wrongly flags
faithfulness model biased toward agreeing with confident language
acceptance_tests: faithfulness score >0.80 on RAGAS benchmark for target domain
extrapolation flagging recall >75% on annotated test set

nodes.definition: Verify mathematical and symbolic reasoning outputs by executing the computation through a symbolic system (sympy, Python, Wolfram), checking numeric equality or symbolic equivalence.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new problem types added or symbolic executor changed

pros.claim: Ground-truth deterministic check for math; no annotation needed
pros.example: 4*sqrt(2) == 5.657 verified exactly by sympy

cons.claim: Only works for computationally tractable math; parsing LLM output is fragile
cons.example: model writes answer in non-standard notation that executor cannot parse

failure_modes: numeric precision mismatch (float vs exact)
model output not parseable by symbolic executor
acceptance_tests: symbolic executor catches 100% of arithmetic errors on injected benchmarks
equivalence check handles algebraic rewrites correctly on test suite
revisit_triggers: equivalence check fails on edge cases

nodes.definition: Run multiple LLM agents that argue for and against candidate answers, aggregating the debate outcome to select the most defensible answer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: agent models change or debate protocol revised

pros.claim: Forces explicit articulation of counter-evidence; surfaces uncertainty
pros.example: debate reveals missing context that single agent ignores

cons.claim: High latency and cost; agents may not genuinely disagree when from same base model
cons.example: GPT-4 vs GPT-4 debate: both convinced of same error

failure_modes: agents echo same wrong answer
sycophantic convergence without genuine debate
acceptance_tests: debate consensus outperforms single-agent by >=3% on contested factual questions
debate produces clear winner on >85% of sessions

nodes.definition: Curate training data and fine-tune a critic model that produces structured critiques (what is wrong, why, how to fix) for LLM outputs in target domain.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: critic quality on new task drops or annotation taxonomy changes

pros.claim: Domain-specific critic outperforms zero-shot GPT-4 critique
pros.example: fine-tuned legal critique model catches contract ambiguities missed by general critic

cons.claim: Expensive annotation; critic may be as expensive as generator to run
cons.example: annotation cost per example $2-5; 10k examples = $20-50k

failure_modes: critic overfits to annotation style
critique vague and non-actionable
acceptance_tests: critic critique quality rated >4/5 by human reviewers on held-out set
critic catch rate for annotated error types >75%

nodes.definition: Monitor and guard against reward hacking: detect when optimized outputs game the verifier or reward model while violating the underlying quality objective.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reward model updated or optimization pressure increases

pros.claim: Prevents silent quality regression behind high reward scores
pros.example: RM score 0.95 but outputs become verbose nonsense; guard triggers audit

cons.claim: Requires ongoing human audit resource; detection lags exploitation
cons.example: weekly audits catch gaming after 7 days of bad outputs already served

failure_modes: gaming undetected until user harm
human audit too infrequent to catch drift
acceptance_tests: human audit detects no systematic reward gaming in sampled outputs
KL divergence from reference policy monitored and capped
revisit_triggers: RM score saturates while task metric stagnates

nodes.definition: Use constrained decoding (grammar-based, regex, or structured output enforcement) to guarantee output format validity, reducing structural hallucinations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: output schema changes or new format required

pros.claim: Eliminates format errors deterministically; downstream parsers never fail
pros.example: API always returns valid JSON even from small models

cons.claim: Constrained to structural validity only; content hallucinations persist inside valid structure
cons.example: valid JSON with hallucinated field values still passes format check

failure_modes: constraint forces grammatically valid but semantically wrong content
decoding library incompatible with model architecture
acceptance_tests: 100% structural validity on outputs constrained to JSON schema
constrained decoding adds <20% latency overhead vs unconstrained

nodes.definition: Run periodic human audits and red-team exercises to discover failure modes not caught by automated verifiers, feeding findings back into verifier improvement and training data.
outputs: training data for new error types

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new deployment domain or user population change

pros.claim: Discovers failure modes automated systems miss; essential for high-risk domains
pros.example: red-team finds medical misinformation pattern not caught by NLI-based verifier

cons.claim: Expensive and slow; findings may not generalize to all user queries
cons.example: red-team of 5 annotators for 2 weeks costs $30k and covers narrow scenario space

failure_modes: red-team lacks domain expertise to find real failures
audit too infrequent relative to model update cadence
acceptance_tests: red-team audit discovers >=3 novel failure modes per quarter
all discovered failure modes logged and triaged within 5 business days

nodes.definition: Measure and monitor calibration quality of LLM confidence estimates over time: expected calibration error (ECE), reliability diagrams, overconfidence/underconfidence detection.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model updated or deployment domain changes

pros.claim: Continuous monitoring catches calibration drift early
pros.example: ECE spike detected week after model update; rollback prevents overconfident hallucinations

cons.claim: Requires labeled ground truth for eval; may not be available in real-time
cons.example: streaming production outputs cannot be labeled fast enough for real-time ECE

failure_modes: evaluation data not representative of deployment distribution
ECE computed on too few samples
acceptance_tests: ECE measured and reported on deployment domain within 2 weeks of model update
calibration monitoring alerts fire within 24h of >0.05 ECE drift

nodes.definition: Systematically diagnose verification failures: categorize error types (factual, logical, format, arithmetic), trace root cause to generator or verifier, prioritize repair actions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new error type emerges or taxonomy revised

pros.claim: Systematic diagnosis prevents repeating the same fix; creates institutional knowledge
pros.example: error taxonomy reveals 60% of failures are format issues, shifting effort from logic to constraint decoding

cons.claim: Taxonomy maintenance overhead; root cause ambiguous when generator and verifier both wrong
cons.example: cannot determine if error is in generator or verifier without controlled ablation

failure_modes: misclassified errors lead to wrong repair
root cause ambiguous between generator and verifier
acceptance_tests: error taxonomy covers >90% of observed failure types
root-cause assignment accuracy >80% on labeled failure sample
revisit_triggers: new error type exceeds 10% of failures

nodes.definition: Verify that LLM outputs are consistent with a formal or semi-formal task specification (requirements doc, schema, business rules), flagging deviations before delivery.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: specification changes or business rules updated

pros.claim: Deterministic rule-based layer catches spec deviations regardless of model behavior
pros.example: financial report: outputs must not contain negative revenue; checker enforces without model knowing

cons.claim: Rules must be manually encoded; spec maintenance burden grows with complexity
cons.example: 100+ business rules require ongoing engineering to encode and test

failure_modes: spec under-specified leaving ambiguity
checker misinterprets rule semantics
acceptance_tests: spec checker detects >90% of injected rule violations in test suite
false positive rate <10% on known-compliant outputs

nodes.definition: Apply specialized calibration and verification for probability and math outputs: check that stated probabilities are coherent, sum to 1 where required, and that confidence intervals are valid.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new probability task type added or user requirement for strict coherence

pros.claim: Absolute requirement for math/probability tasks; incoherent probabilities are incorrect by definition
pros.example: P(A)+P(not A)=0.8 caught and rejected before financial decision

cons.claim: Only syntactic coherence; coherent probabilities can still be factually wrong
cons.example: P(heads)=0.5, P(tails)=0.5 is coherent but model may have wrong prior

failure_modes: model outputs probabilities summing to !=1 and goes undetected
model confident but incoherent probability assignments
acceptance_tests: 100% of probability outputs pass coherence check (sum-to-one, non-negative)
confidence interval validity rate >98% on test suite
revisit_triggers: user domain expanded to finance or actuarial

conflict_axes.description: Higher-quality verifiers (PRM, fine-tuned critics) dramatically reduce error rates but multiply inference cost and latency.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use PRM for high-stakes math/science; ORM for lower-stakes preference tasks; heuristics only for low-risk format checks

conflict_axes.description: Self-refine loops can amplify initial errors if the model's critique is miscalibrated, producing worse outputs than no refinement.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: limit iterations to 3; always compare refined output to original before committing; abort if verifier score drops

conflict_axes.description: PRM provides fine-grained step supervision but requires expensive step annotations; ORM scales cheaply but cannot localize errors.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use PRM for formal reasoning domains (math, code) where steps are unambiguous; ORM for open-ended generation

conflict_axes.description: Setting abstention thresholds too conservatively reduces hallucinations but increases refusals, frustrating users on near-threshold queries.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: calibrate threshold per domain risk level; medical=strict, general QA=lenient; monitor abstention rate as KPI

conflict_axes.description: Tool-grounded checks are highly reliable for verifiable claims but add latency; not all claims are tool-verifiable.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: apply tool verification only to claim types with available deterministic oracles; cache tool results where possible

conflict_axes.description: Heavy optimization pressure (many RLHF steps) exploits reward model weaknesses faster than guards can detect; guard must be tighter as optimization intensifies.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: gate each RL training phase with human audit; limit KL divergence per phase; stop when human preference diverges from RM score

conflict_axes.description: High-recall hallucination detection flags too many true claims as unsupported; high-precision misses subtle hallucinations.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: tune threshold by domain risk; high-risk (medical, legal): recall priority; low-risk: precision priority

conflict_axes.description: Automated verifiers scale but miss novel failure modes; human audits discover new failures but are slow and expensive.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: automate for known error types; mandatory human audit at model update boundaries and on high-risk domains

conflict_axes.description: Constrained decoding and spec checking ensure structural validity but cannot verify semantic correctness; NLI/PRM verify semantics but not structure.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: layer both: constrained decoding first (cheap), then semantic verification on structurally valid outputs

conflict_axes.description: Best-of-N and self-refine consume inference compute; PRM/ORM training consumes training compute; budget may not support both.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: prefer inference-time methods when training data is scarce; shift to PRM when annotation pipeline established

edge_cases.title: Verifier Shares Generator Bias
edge_cases.description: Verifier trained on same data as generator fails to catch systematic errors both learned; e.g. both hallucinate the same wrong date.
edge_cases.trigger_condition: verifier and generator share pretraining corpus
edge_cases.recommended_action: train verifier on distinct data; use external tool-grounded check as independent oracle

edge_cases.title: Self-Refine Divergence
edge_cases.description: Self-refine loop makes output progressively worse because critique is miscalibrated; iteration 3 is worse than iteration 1.
edge_cases.recommended_action: implement monotone stopping: abort if score does not improve over 2 consecutive iterations

edge_cases.title: PRM Step Boundary Ambiguity
edge_cases.description: Annotators cannot agree on where one reasoning step ends and another begins; labels are noisy and harm PRM quality.
edge_cases.recommended_action: define explicit step segmentation grammar; use structured CoT format with delimiters

edge_cases.title: Reward Hacking Saturation
edge_cases.description: ORM score saturates near 1.0 while human preference drops; model has gamed the verifier without tripping Goodhart guard.
edge_cases.trigger_condition: RM score >0.95 but human eval drops >5%
edge_cases.recommended_action: trigger immediate human audit; reduce optimization steps; consider RM retraining

edge_cases.title: Tool Unavailability at Inference
edge_cases.description: Tool-grounded checker fails because external API is down; pipeline defaults to unverified output delivery.
edge_cases.trigger_condition: tool API returns error or timeout
edge_cases.recommended_action: implement fallback: flag output as unverified rather than silently passing; cache recent tool results

edge_cases.title: Calibration Domain Shift
edge_cases.description: Temperature-scaled model is well-calibrated on validation domain but over-confident on new deployment domain.
edge_cases.trigger_condition: ECE on new domain >0.10 after deployment
edge_cases.recommended_action: recalibrate on representative new-domain data before deployment; monitor ECE per domain

edge_cases.title: Majority Vote on Correlated Errors
edge_cases.description: Self-consistency majority vote returns wrong answer confidently because all chains share same systematic bias.
edge_cases.trigger_condition: all K chains reach same conclusion with high similarity
edge_cases.recommended_action: sample with higher temperature or use diverse prompts; verify via tool oracle if available

edge_cases.title: Spec Underspecification
edge_cases.description: Spec consistency checker cannot flag violations because the specification is ambiguous or incomplete.
edge_cases.recommended_action: spec review before checker deployment; require formal spec with examples for each rule

edge_cases.title: Incoherent Probability Output Not Caught
edge_cases.description: Model outputs probabilities summing to 1.3 but coherence checker was not included in pipeline; downstream decision model uses bad inputs.
edge_cases.trigger_condition: probability coherence checker absent from pipeline
edge_cases.recommended_action: make coherence check mandatory gate for any probability output task

edge_cases.title: Human Audit Expertise Gap
edge_cases.description: Red-team auditors lack domain expertise to recognize subtle errors in specialized domains (medical, legal, quantitative finance).
edge_cases.trigger_condition: audit team has no domain specialists
edge_cases.recommended_action: hire or contract domain experts for audit; use structured checklists covering known failure categories

edge_cases.title: Hallucination Detection False Positive Cascade
edge_cases.description: High-recall NLI model flags correct claims as hallucinated; downstream system rejects valid outputs at high rate, degrading user experience.
edge_cases.trigger_condition: false positive rate >20% on known-correct outputs
edge_cases.recommended_action: tune NLI threshold; use ensemble of NLI models; human review false positive samples

edge_cases.title: Constrained Decoding Semantic Trap
edge_cases.description: Grammar-constrained output is structurally valid but semantically nonsensical because constraint forced wrong token choice.
edge_cases.trigger_condition: constrained output passes format check but fails semantic review
edge_cases.recommended_action: add semantic validation layer after structural constraint; allow model to abstain if no valid completion found

workflow.description: Identify which output types require verification (factual claims, math, probabilities, structure, code) and map to appropriate verifier strategies.
Implement structural constraints (JSON schema, grammar) as first verification layer; eliminates format errors at zero annotation cost.
Wire up calculator, code executor, and retrieval oracle for claim types that have deterministic ground truth.
workflow.gate: tool verification recall >80% on injected error benchmark

workflow.description: Choose ORM (outcome) or PRM (process) based on task and annotation budget; train on labeled data; validate on held-out split.
workflow.gate: reward model eval metric passes threshold

workflow.description: Apply temperature scaling; measure ECE on validation domain; set abstention threshold per domain risk level.
Build NLI-based and RAG-grounding hallucination pipeline; tune precision-recall tradeoff for domain risk level.
Elicit structured CoT; apply step-level verification using PRM or symbolic checker; validate against math/reasoning benchmarks.
workflow.gate: error detection rate >65% on reasoning benchmark

workflow.description: Deploy inference-time compute strategy (self-refine or best-of-N) based on latency budget and verifier quality.
workflow.gate: quality improvement over single-pass baseline confirmed

workflow.description: Set up KL divergence monitoring, RM score tracking, and human audit trigger conditions; mandatory before any RLHF optimization.
workflow.gate: human audit cadence and trigger conditions documented and approved

workflow.description: Continuously collect verification failures; categorize by type; root-cause to generator or verifier; prioritize repairs; feed back to critic training.
workflow.gate: error taxonomy covers >90% of observed failure types

workflow.description: Monitor ECE and abstention rate in production; trigger recalibration on domain shift; run probability coherence checks continuously.
workflow.gate: ECE alert fires within 24h of >0.05 drift

dominance_rules.rule: PRM dominates ORM for mathematical and multi-step reasoning tasks when step annotations are feasible
dominance_rules.condition: task requires step-level error localization (math, code, formal reasoning)
dominance_rules.rationale: ORM cannot localize errors in long chains; PRM provides actionable step feedback

dominance_rules.rule: Tool-grounded verification dominates NLI-based checking for numeric and arithmetic claims
dominance_rules.condition: claim is numeric, algebraic, or computationally verifiable
dominance_rules.rationale: deterministic executor provides ground truth; NLI model may hallucinate entailment

dominance_rules.rule: Calibrated abstention dominates forced response for high-risk domains
dominance_rules.condition: domain is medical, legal, or financial and confidence below threshold
dominance_rules.rationale: confident wrong answer causes more harm than acknowledged uncertainty in high-stakes domains

dominance_rules.rule: Constrained decoding dominates post-hoc format fixing for structural requirements
dominance_rules.condition: output format must be machine-parseable (JSON, SQL, XML)
dominance_rules.rationale: post-hoc repair is fragile; constrained decoding guarantees validity at token level

dominance_rules.rule: Human audit dominates automated verifier alone for novel failure mode discovery
dominance_rules.condition: first deployment in a new domain or after major model update
dominance_rules.rationale: automated verifiers only catch known error types; human audit required for unknown-unknown failure modes

dominance_rules.rule: Self-consistency dominates self-refine when critique quality is uncertain
dominance_rules.condition: model critique reliability unknown or unvalidated
dominance_rules.rationale: self-consistency requires only sampling, not reliable critique; self-refine fails when critique is miscalibrated

dominance_rules.rule: Goodhart guard is mandatory when cumulative RL optimization exceeds 3 training phases
dominance_rules.condition: RL has run more than 3 phases on same reward model without human re-evaluation
dominance_rules.rationale: reward hacking likelihood increases super-linearly with optimization pressure; guard is not optional

dominance_rules.rule: PRM-guided best-of-N dominates ORM-guided best-of-N on multi-step reasoning tasks
dominance_rules.condition: task involves multi-step reasoning with intermediate states
dominance_rules.rationale: PRM uses step-level quality signal for selection, not only final answer correctness

dominance_rules.rule: RAG faithfulness verification dominates open-web hallucination detection for RAG systems
dominance_rules.condition: system uses RAG and has identifiable source passages
dominance_rules.rationale: RAG verify can use passage entailment; hallucination detect without source is weaker and less targeted

dominance_rules.rule: Probability coherence check is a mandatory blocking gate for any probability output
dominance_rules.condition: output contains stated probabilities or probability distributions
dominance_rules.rationale: incoherent probabilities are logically impossible; no downstream reasoning should proceed on them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not train a new verifier without first profiling error types from production
anti_rework_rules.rationale: training verifier on wrong error distribution wastes annotation budget

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not tune PRM step boundaries without first establishing inter-annotator agreement baseline
anti_rework_rules.rationale: low IAA produces noisy labels that harm PRM training; measure first

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy RLHF optimization without activating Goodhart guard first
anti_rework_rules.rationale: reward gaming detected after deployment requires costly rollback

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not select self-refine vs self-consistency without measuring critique reliability first
anti_rework_rules.rationale: self-refine underperforms self-consistency when critique is miscalibrated; measurement avoids wrong choice

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not measure ECE on wrong distribution; calibration eval data must match deployment domain
anti_rework_rules.rationale: domain-mismatched calibration gives false confidence; recalibration required again after deployment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not implement spec consistency checker before formalizing the spec with examples
anti_rework_rules.rationale: ambiguous spec leads to incorrect checker implementation requiring full rebuild

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run hallucination detection without first tuning NLI threshold on domain data
anti_rework_rules.rationale: default NLI threshold causes excessive false positives on domain-specific language

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy math verification without testing symbolic executor on edge cases (floats, special functions)
anti_rework_rules.rationale: precision mismatches discovered post-deployment require emergency fixes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not scale best-of-N beyond N=8 without profiling verifier quality first
anti_rework_rules.rationale: high N with bad verifier multiplies cost without quality gain; profile at N=4,8 first

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip red-team audit when deploying to new user population or domain
anti_rework_rules.rationale: automated verifiers trained on prior domain miss novel failure modes in new population

iteration_protocol.trigger: verifier catch-rate drops below 70% on evaluation benchmark
iteration_protocol.action: audit verifier training data distribution; retrain with additional negatives from recent failure log

iteration_protocol.trigger: self-refine loop converges to worse output on >10% of inputs
iteration_protocol.action: reduce max iterations to 2; evaluate if critique prompt requires revision; consider switching to self-consistency

iteration_protocol.trigger: PRM step annotation IAA falls below 0.70
iteration_protocol.action: revise step segmentation guidelines; retrain annotators; revalidate PRM on clean annotation sample

iteration_protocol.trigger: Goodhart guard detects RM score >0.95 with human eval drop >5%
iteration_protocol.action: halt optimization; trigger full human audit; retrain or replace reward model

iteration_protocol.trigger: ECE exceeds 0.08 on any deployment domain
iteration_protocol.action: run temperature scaling recalibration on domain-representative validation set; adjust abstention threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: hallucination detection false positive rate exceeds 20%
iteration_protocol.action: retune NLI threshold; consider ensemble of NLI models; add domain-specific positive examples to calibration set

iteration_protocol.trigger: math verification fails to parse >5% of model outputs
iteration_protocol.action: fix output format prompt; update symbolic executor parser; add parser regression tests

iteration_protocol.trigger: error diagnosis reveals new error type exceeding 10% of failures
iteration_protocol.action: extend error taxonomy; add annotated examples to critic training data; update spec consistency checker

iteration_protocol.trigger: best-of-N quality gain falls below 2% vs N=1
iteration_protocol.action: investigate verifier quality; consider verifier retraining; evaluate alternative selection strategy

priority_rationale: VERIF_FRAMEWORK anchors all downstream; tool/hallucination/PRM/Goodhart address highest-risk failure modes first; inference-time and structural checks follow; monitoring and diagnosis complete the cycle.

structural_checks: priority_order contains all node ids exactly once
reference_checks: all competency_question_refs resolve to competency_questions ids
all conflict_axis_refs in traceability resolve to conflict_axes
obligation_checks: high risk_if_wrong nodes have acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have resolution_rule and signed_tension<0
